about: check reports, as build does and before any input is read, each read that binding refuses from the declarations alone (#3542, #2844 decision 3; #3552, #3580, #3585, #3678): a root filter's read of another dataset or of a column (NAME-3, ROW-9), reported once every column and the column order are bound; a flag's or case predicate's qualifier that nothing declares (FORMULA-9); a formula in a case result of a specification without rows, which reads only lookups and columns (NAME-3); each read of a lookup whose key types fail, which binding does not bind (LOOKUP-9); a row template filter's field qualified by nothing declared (NAME-3); the operands a formula reads, typed once its names bind (FORMULA-12); every other read of a field qualified by nothing declared (NAME-3, FORMULA-9, LOOKUP-9); the reads of a lookup binding binds without its derivations, which it admits for no row (LOOKUP-15, LOOKUP-17); a text extraction's or replacement's source that is not text and, once binding takes its source, its pattern and group (TEXT-1, TEXT-6, TEXT-10); an aggregate filter's read outside what the aggregate reduces (NAME-3); and a lookup filter's field qualified by nothing declared where the declarations decide the finding's suggestion (LOOKUP-7, D220). Each case runs check and build for the default host, since a request without a project reads no environment entry, and both report its rows. Where only the records decide a finding, check leaves it to build, whose issues check's stay a subsequence of (D195, D199), so check and build are each a case. The specification is the document implicit (no rows, VS the base), record (one row template over VS) or grouped (one row template over VS grouped by subject). Each declares the inputs VS, HOME without a key, PLAN and DM, and the lookups PL, whose key types fail (DOSENUM, an int, matches the str USUBJID), and PB, a filtered lookup that binds; X derives 0.0 and C derives 'A' unless an edit replaces them. A case writes the files its specification names. Moved from check_unknown_reads.rs, whose tests compared each issue's spec paths in order, the first issue's condition and rule, for some also its spec paths and context, and check's issues with build's: a case states every issue's spec paths, and where there are several, the case ending _first_issue states the first of them by what its test compared of it: as the first issue reported (`prefix`) where a later issue has its spec paths too, and otherwise among the issues, which the complete case's spec paths, held by no later issue, already place first.
